questions.q: What are the causes and consequences of migration in India?

answer.text: Migration is caused by push and pull factors. Push factors force people to leave a place, such as poverty, unemployment, poor living conditions, and natural disasters in the villages. Pull factors attract people to another place, such as jobs, higher wages, better education, health care and the amenities of cities. In India, men migrate mainly in search of work, while women migrate largely on account of marriage.

Migration has mixed effects. Economically, migrants send back remittances that help their families and villages, though the source areas may suffer a loss of skilled workers, a brain drain. Demographically, it redistributes population and swells cities. Socially, it mixes cultures but can also create slums, overcrowding and tension. It puts heavy pressure on urban housing, water and services.

answer: Thus migration reshapes both the places people leave and the places they move to.
